bull.b: Sequential growth in product revenue and prescriptions indicates that VIZZ is gaining commercial traction after launch. If this momentum persists, expanding patient adoption can improve operating leverage, support broader distribution, and strengthen LENZ’s position in the presbyopia treatment market.

A leading share position, supported by more than 15,000 prescribing eye-care professionals and high repeat-prescriber participation, provides an important foundation for durable growth. It may also improve the efficiency of future consumer marketing and commercial expansion.

Essentially no debt reduces financial risk and preserves flexibility while LENZ restructures its cost base. The planned expense reduction, if delivered, could materially lower cash requirements and allow more of the remaining budget to support consumer acquisition and product growth.

bear.b: The combination of shrinking revenue, widening losses, and substantial negative cash flow shows that the commercial base has not yet reached sufficient scale to fund operations. Continued spending at this level could require additional financing and limit strategic flexibility.

A CEO transition during a major commercial reorganization creates execution uncertainty at an important stage of VIZZ’s launch. Interim leadership and an open-ended search for a permanent CEO could slow decisions, disrupt accountability, or weaken continuity across strategic initiatives.

Because the category is still developing, LENZ must continue educating patients and clinicians before demand becomes broadly established. That can lengthen the path to sustainable scale, require disciplined marketing investment, and make future adoption less predictable than in mature eye-care markets.
